blocks.text: I’m Amanda D’Souza. I have been teaching science for more than 25 years, and my career has taken me through Canada, Japan, Australia, England, Egypt, Barbados, Qatar and Vietnam. I spent about 20 years living and working internationally, teaching students from many backgrounds and working within different school systems. That has given me a broad view of education and shown me something practical: a student can move from one school or curriculum to another and suddenly appear to have “gaps” simply because the sequence, terminology or expectations have changed. I understand how important it is to find those gaps without turning them into a judgement about the student’s ability.

blocks.label: P: Over the years I have taught IB Diploma Biology, Chemistry and Environmental Sys
blocks.text: Over the years I have taught IB Diploma Biology, Chemistry and Environmental Systems and Societies; IB MYP Science; the International Middle Years Curriculum; GCSE and IGCSE Biology and Chemistry, including Combined and Coordinated Science; AS and A-Level Biology; and Ontario secondary science. I have also led science departments in Vietnam and Barbados and worked in curriculum development, assessment and teacher mentoring. Since 2013, I have worked as an IB Biology Assistant Examiner, with experience assessing HL Paper 2 and Internal Assessments against IB criteria. That work has given me a close understanding of how IB assessment criteria are applied and, importantly, of the difference between knowing the science and communicating that knowledge effectively under assessment conditions.

blocks.label: H2: Biology, education and professional certification.
P: My academic background is in Biology. I completed my Bachelor of Science in
blocks.text: My academic background is in Biology. I completed my Bachelor of Science in Biology at the University of Western Ontario in London, Ontario, in 2000. I then moved to Australia for teacher training, completing a Diploma of Education at the University of Wollongong in New South Wales in 2002. I am an Ontario Certified Teacher (OCT #496538), hold Qualified Teacher Status in England, and have completed Guidance and Career Education Additional Qualification Parts 1 and 2.

P: Those qualifications and years of experience matter, but they are not the whole
blocks.text: Those qualifications and years of experience matter, but they are not the whole of good tutoring. For me, the starting point is the student. I want students to be comfortable saying when they do not understand something, because there is no value in nodding along to an explanation that has not landed. I use conversation, questions and carefully chosen tasks to see what a student understands, and I change the pace or approach when the evidence tells me to.

blocks.text: I believe students can be challenged and supported at the same time. I will be honest about what needs work, help turn a large goal into manageable next steps and expect the student to take an active part in the process. Ultimately, I want students to understand more and trust themselves more — to become increasingly able to work things out without waiting for someone else to tell them what to do.
